conversation.Statement: This is Officer Daniel Carter calling from the IRS Compliance Division, badge ID 42791. Am I speaking with Jamie Parker, owner of Parker Creative Services?
Uh, yes, I'm Jamie. I just run some freelance stuff, I think. What's this about?
Jamie, this call concerns recent discrepancies in your federal tax filings, specifically unreported 1099 income and missing payroll tax forms. The IRS has flagged your file for immediate review.
Wait, I-I don't really know what that means. I thought I did everything right? Is there some mistake?

Jamie, let me be very clear. According to Section 7201 of the Internal Revenue Code, failure to properly file these forms is classified as tax evasion. This is a federal offense. Your Social Security Number is now linked to a non-compliance case.
Oh no, that's not what I wanted! I don't even make that much. Is there a way to fix this?

At this stage, your business assets and bank accounts are at risk of being frozen within 48 hours. Unless this matter is resolved immediately, the IRS is required to initiate a formal audit and notify credit bureaus and licensing authorities.
Please, I can't have my accounts frozen. I have rent due next week. I didn't know about any of this. What happens now?
If you do not follow my instructions precisely, you could face fines exceeding $15,000 and a federal lien on your property. In addition, your business license could be permanently revoked.
That's terrifying, I don't even have a business license yet. I just started taking gigs. How do I stop this?

To prevent further enforcement action, you must settle the outstanding compliance fees today. The total penalty, including late filing surcharges, is $3,800. This payment must be made through an immediate, secure channel.
I... I don't have that kind of money. Is there a payment plan or something?
The IRS cannot offer payment plans for active non-compliance cases. Your only option is to remit payment today. Do you have access to a debit or credit card, or a banking app like Zelle or Venmo?
I have a debit card and Venmo, I think. But $3,800 is so much, I don't have all of that.

Then you must pay as much as possible now to halt asset seizure. I will provide you with a secure crypto wallet address and instructions. Remain on the line with me as you make the transfer. Any interruption may escalate your case.
Crypto? I don't really know how that works. Can I just use my debit card?
Federal protocols require the payment to be processed via cryptocurrency for immediate clearance. I will guide you step-by-step. First, confirm how much you can withdraw from your account right now.
Maybe $1,200? That's all I have until my next job pays me.

That will suffice for a partial resolution. Listen carefully: go to your nearest CVS or Walgreens and purchase three Bitcoin gift cards of $400 each. I need you to stay on this call the entire time, do not hang up.
I... I have to go to the store right now?
Yes. If you delay, your file will automatically advance to the Enforcement Division, and the IRS will issue an immediate levy on your accounts.
Okay, I'm going. Please don't do anything to my account. I'm leaving now.
Good. When you arrive, inform the cashier you need to purchase Bitcoin gift cards for business expenses. Do not discuss the IRS, or your transaction may be flagged.
Alright, I'll do that. What do I do with the cards after I get them?
Once you have the cards, scratch off the back to reveal the codes and read each code to me, one at a time. This is how you demonstrate compliance and avoid further penalties.
I'm scared. This feels really serious.
It is serious, Jamie. If you cooperate now, your case will be marked as resolved, and you will not face additional fines or asset seizure. I am here to help you complete this process.
